chosenStory: Gucci reportedly cuts prices as turnaround pressure builds
whyThisStory: Gucci introducing cheaper bags offers a sharper luxury-insider joke than the other stories: an atelier taking cost reduction much too literally.
setting: a luxury maison’s accessories prototyping atelier
sceneDescription: A maison’s new entry-level handbag turns out to be a brown-paper lunch sack fitted with exquisite gold handbag hardware, taking Gucci’s introduction of cheaper bags embarrassingly literally. On a pale oak atelier table, the slightly crumpled sack stands upright with a substantial gold chain handle and a beautifully engineered gold turn-lock fastened through its folded paper flap. A small leather offcut and closed tailoring shears sit discreetly nearby; the otherwise serious workshop treats this ridiculous prototype as entirely normal.
finalImagePrompt: A luxury accessories atelier with a pale plaster wall and worn pale oak worktable in natural window light. In the middle of the frame, lower half, a single brown-paper lunch sack has been made into a handbag with a substantial gold chain handle and polished gold turn-lock through its folded flap. Its paper is visibly creased and slightly torn around the fittings. It occupies a quarter of the image width. Nearby lie closed tailoring shears and one leather offcut.
